exercises.text: Which molecules move faster in the atmosphere: hydrogen molecules or nitrogen molecules?
How does the internal energy of an ideal gas change during processes $1-1'$ and $1'-2$ in Figure $24$? How does it change during processes $1-2$, $2-3$, and $3-1$ in Figure $30$?

At standard atmospheric pressure and a temperature of $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$, which contains more molecules: the air in a room of volume $50$ m$^3$, or the water in a glass holding $200$ cm$^3$ of water?
By what percentage does the mean-square speed of water molecules in our blood increase when the temperature rises from $37^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $40^\circ\mathrm{C}$?

Modern vacuum pumps can reduce pressure to $1.3\times10^{-10}$ N/m$^2$, approximately $10^{-12}$ mm of mercury. At this pressure and a temperature of $27^\circ\mathrm{C}$, how many gas molecules are contained in $1$ cm$^3$?

$4$ moles of a monatomic ideal gas are compressed in a compressor cylinder. Find how much the gas temperature rises during one stroke if the work done during that stroke is $500$ J. Assume the process is adiabatic.
